Great work on the CP/M polish! Re: your question — yes, the Z3 solver handles exactly those cases:

1. **Loops with pointer arithmetic**: Z3 uses per-instruction location variables (lv{vreg}_i{inst}), so it tracks register state through loops correctly. The CFG solver adds edge constraints between loop head and body exit — no stale HL values. Production PBQP solves per-block independently which is why it loses cross-block state.

2. **u16 multiply + constants**: VIR inlines mul16 per call site with Z3-chosen registers. No fixed ABI (HL×DE), so constants can stay where they are. Production pins HL/DE which forces unnecessary moves.

3. **HL→IX forwarding**: Z3 has IXH/IXL as first-class spill locations (8T vs 11T PUSH/POP). It can keep values in IX halves across calls without the HL forwarding hack.

The path to fixing production: the --vir flag already works for standalone compilation. For your CP/M screen code, you could try compiling with --vir and see if the inline asm workarounds become unnecessary. The Z3 solver treats OpAsmBlock as an opaque black box with clobbers — surrounding code stays fully optimized.
